vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: To not be at work, because of a holiday or a day off
To collect somebody or something from a place
An informal meeting of friends or family, usually at somebody home
The moment a football match starts
The time you spend in an airport between two flights
A weekend with an extra day off because of a holiday
To manage to arrive or to be somewhere as planned

vocab.text: Notice the pair: to run late is the problem, and not to make it is the result. You can run late and still make it, and that is the whole story of a Saturday morning.

items: A colleague from another country asks what you are doing this weekend. Give four arrangements with times, and one thing you are not doing.
Somebody wants to meet you on Saturday. Find a window together: say when you are busy, when you are free, and agree on a time and a place.
Describe an ordinary Saturday morning in your family as if it were happening right now, hour by hour, from waking up to lunch.

practice.title: Say each plan again in the form the cue asks for.
items: go to the match on Saturday
at ten on Saturday, watch the match
this time next week, fly home

items.situation: A colleague asks what you are doing at the weekend. Answer with three arrangements and a time for each.
tips: Fixed plans take the present continuous: I am taking, we are having.
A plan with no time is not an arrangement. Give the hour.

items.situation: They ask whether you are free on Saturday afternoon. You are not, until four.
tips: Say what you are doing, not just no.
Then offer the window you do have.

items.situation: They ask what you will be doing at nine on Saturday morning.
tips: A picture of a moment: I will be watching...
The time expression comes first or last, never in the middle.

items.situation: The traffic is terrible and you are going to arrive after kick-off. Call and say so.
tips: I am running late, and the evidence is in front of you: going to.
Give a new time, not an apology.

items.situation: They ask what you are doing on the Monday of the long weekend.
tips: I am off. Then say what you are doing with the day.
Finish with a question back about their holiday.

answerkey.title: Reveal the model answers
list: I am going to the match on Saturday.
At ten on Saturday I will be watching the match.
We are having a get-together at one.
This time next week I will be flying home.
answerkey.note: The present continuous is an appointment already in the diary. will be doing is a photograph of a moment that has not arrived yet.

listenings.text: Hi Felipe, this is Bea from the club. Two changes for Saturday. We are playing at nine in the morning, not at eleven, because the other team is travelling from Campinas. Kick-off is at nine sharp, so the girls are arriving at a quarter past eight. And we are not using the usual field. We are playing on field three, behind the parking. One more thing. I am collecting the shirts after the match, so please do not take them home this time. If you are running late, send me a message and we will start without her.

Felipe, it is Lars. My flight lands on Thursday evening, so I am not coming to the office on Friday morning. I am sleeping. On Friday afternoon I am meeting your team at the distribution center, and on Saturday I am completely free. So, two questions. Are you going to the match on Saturday, and is there a spare ticket? I have never seen a game in Brazil and I am not leaving without one. And on Sunday I have a nine hour layover in Lisbon on the way home, which is a long time to sit in an airport. If you know anybody there, tell me. This time next week I will be sitting in that terminal thinking about it.

extra_audio.text: First, Lars asks what Felipe is doing on Saturday. Then Felipe says he is taking his daughter to her match and that kick-off is at nine. After that, he explains that they are having a get-together at his sister house until four. Next, Lars asks about the game in the evening and Felipe offers to get him a ticket. Finally, they agree to meet at seven, and Lars promises to send a message if he is running late.
